price_basis: Indicative installed costs, GBP, 2023-2026 prices. Secondary sources citing the Energy Saving Trust, RICS and MCS; real quotes vary widely. Shown as ranges, never as quotes.

stages.3: Low-carbon heating: sized for the improved home
stages.4: Generation: sized for the new electricity demand

loft_insulation.name: Loft insulation top-up to 270 mm
loft_insulation.cost_source: EST via Rightmove (semi-detached avg ~GBP 930, July 2023 prices); HOA (~GBP 825)

conditions: The home has its own roof space (not a flat with a dwelling above)
Existing loft insulation below 200 mm
High suitability at 100 mm or less, Medium above that or when the depth is assumed

cavity_wall_insulation.name: Cavity wall insulation
cavity_wall_insulation.cost_source: NerdWallet citing typical semi-detached ~GBP 2,700; Which? (RICS cost data, Nov 2024)

conditions: Cavity walls, not already insulated
High suitability when wall type and insulation are recorded; Medium when inferred from construction age (survey confirms)

solid_wall_insulation.name: Solid wall insulation (internal or external)
solid_wall_insulation.cost_source: Industry ranges for internal (lower) and external (higher) wall insulation; highly variable

conditions: Solid walls, not already insulated
Medium suitability (cost and disruption); Low in a listed building or conservation area (consent)

glazing_upgrade.name: Upgrade to modern double glazing
glazing_upgrade.cost_source: Typical UK market ranges (GBP 400-800 per window)

conditions: Single, secondary or pre-2002 double glazing
High for single, Medium for secondary, Low for pre-2002 double or in a listed building

smart_controls.name: Smart thermostat and heating controls
smart_controls.evidence_note: Published trials report anywhere from about 0% to 10%; 5% is a central assumption and is marked uncertain.

conditions: A wet (boiler or heat pump) heating system without smart controls
Not modelled for electric storage/direct heaters (they need heater-level controls)

air_source_heat_pump.name: Air source heat pump
air_source_heat_pump.cost_source: EST (~GBP 14,000 installed), EDF (~GBP 13,000 average), before grant
air_source_heat_pump.grant_note: Boiler Upgrade Scheme: up to GBP 7,500 in England and Wales (Home Energy Scotland offers similar). Eligibility is not assessed here.
air_source_heat_pump.evidence_note: BUS requires a minimum SCOP of 2.8; monitored UK installations often achieve more. Leaky homes need higher flow temperatures and achieve lower SCOP.

conditions: Not already heat-pump heated; outdoor space for the external unit
Suitability from the heat loss per m² AFTER the recommended fabric measures: High up to 2.0 W/K·m², Medium up to 2.8, Low above
One step more suitable when replacing electric storage/direct heating; one step less when outdoor space is unrecorded
Depends on the recommended fabric measures being done first

ps2_illustrative_impact.quantity: purchased energy (electricity use may rise as gas use falls)

solar_pv.name: Solar PV panels
solar_pv.cost_source: MCS installation data (~GBP 2,193 per kW, 2023); 2026 market quotes ~GBP 5,000-7,000 for 4 kWp
solar_pv.evidence_note: Typical UK yield is roughly 800-1,000 kWh per kWp per year depending on location, orientation and shading.

conditions: No existing PV; a roof that is not north-facing
Flats: infeasible unless top floor, where roof access needs the freeholder's consent (check first)
Listed building or conservation area: needs consent (check first), not ruled out
High for south-facing, Medium east/west or unknown orientation, Low with heavy shading
Sized after a heat pump, because the heat pump raises daytime electricity demand

impact_note: ps2_illustrative_impact quotes the brief's illustrative table (PS2 §4) verbatim: each row refers to its own quantity and they are not additive. Per PS2 §4 this catalogue's engineering parameters take precedence; reports/RETROFIT_IMPACTS.md sets the engine's modelled impact on the same quantity beside these ranges and beside measured savings in real UK homes (DESNZ NEED).
